answer: Attention Ledger Pruning: each identity must sustain a minimum weekly interaction count with a rotating set of counterparties, tracked in a shared garden of active peers. Missed quotas trigger pruning, forcing the identity to re-earn visibility from zero. The weekly anchor is a published digest of sustained exchanges, and a yarrow score weights rare counterparties higher, so farming cheap repeated pairs yields little. An attacker must fund continuous distinct interactions across many peers for weeks, making each fake identity cost real attention-hours, not one-time fees.
